title: كَانَ and Its Sisters
lede: Move nominal sentences into a past frame, describe past habits and show how situations became or remained.

items.prompt: Transform “The weather is beautiful” into the past.
items.feedback: كَانَ keeps its noun nominative and makes a single-word predicate accusative.
كُنْتُ is the first-person singular form.
The feminine form is كَانَتْ and the predicate is accusative.

items.prompt: Which expresses a repeated past habit?
items.feedback: كَانَ + present commonly expresses an ongoing or habitual past action.
صَارَ works like كَانَ and expresses becoming.

items.prompt: Which means “The problem is still difficult”?
items.feedback: مَا زَالَ expresses continuation: still.
كُنَّا is “we were”; human masculine/mixed plural predicate is accusative ـين.

items.prompt: Choose “The teachers (f.) were in the hall.”
items.feedback: Verb-first formal agreement is singular feminine before the overt plural subject; prepositional predicate is unchanged.
Subject-first human feminine plural takes full agreement: كُنَّ.
ظَلَّ takes an accusative single-word predicate.

items.prompt: What does كَانَ add to a present nominal sentence?
options: A past state or past frame
items.feedback: كَانَ places the state in the past.
Ism kāna nominative; single-word khabar accusative.
First-person singular is كُنْتُ.
كَانُوا + accusative human plural predicate.
The prepositional predicate remains governed by فِي.

items.prompt: Which means “I used to study in the evening”?
items.feedback: كَانَ + present gives a past habitual/ongoing frame.
صَارَ expresses change into a new state.
ظَلَّ expresses continuation and follows the kāna pattern.

items.prompt: Which means “The school is still open”?
items.feedback: مَا زَالَ needs مَا and follows the kāna pattern.

options: Is the state in the correct time frame, and is the predicate formed correctly?
Did I make every following word accusative?
Did I add ال to the predicate?
items.feedback: Only the relevant noun/predicate relationship changes; prepositional phrases keep their own government.

games.e: Past state: noun nominative, predicate accusative.

games.p: We used to play after school.
games.e: كَانَ + present creates a past habitual frame.

games.p: The students were in the library.
games.e: Formal verb-first agreement is singular before an overt plural subject.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَسْتَعْمِلُ كَانَ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا؟
These verbs move a nominal sentence into the past or show becoming and continuing states.
### Core
Use كَانَ with identity, description and location.
### Develop
Conjugate كَانَ and use it with a present verb for past habits.
### Stretch
Use صَارَ, ظَلَّ and مَا زَالَ with case-aware control.
[callout] Communication target: describe how people, places and routines were in the past and how situations changed or continued.
## Diagnostic start
Test meaning, conjugation and the core case pattern.
## From present state to past state
كَانَ enters the nominal sentence and places it in a past frame.

TABLE: Present | Past with كَانَ | Meaning // الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ. | كَانَ الْجَوُّ بَارِدًا. | The weather was cold. // أَحْمَدُ طَالِبٌ. | كَانَ أَحْمَدُ طَالِبًا. | Ahmad was a student. // مَرْيَمُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. | كَانَتْ مَرْيَمُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. | Maryam was at home.
[callout] Case-aware pattern: كَانَ + اسْمُهَا الْمَرْفُوعُ + خَبَرُهَا الْمَنْصُوبُ . A prepositional predicate keeps the case required by its preposition.
## Conjugating كَانَ
The form changes with the person, gender and number of the subject.

TABLE: Subject | Form | Model // أنا | كُنْتُ | كُنْتُ مُتْعَبَةً. // أنتَ / أنتِ | كُنْتَ / كُنْتِ | كُنْتِ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ. // هو | كَانَ | كَانَ مُسْتَعِدًّا. // هي | كَانَتْ | كَانَتْ مُسْتَعِدَّةً. // نحن | كُنَّا | كُنَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ. // هم | كَانُوا | كَانُوا مُجْتَهِدِينَ. // هنّ | كُنَّ | كُنَّ مُجْتَهِدَاتٍ.
[callout/warning] Word-order link: كَانَ الطُّلَّابُ مُسْتَعِدِّينَ is formal verb-first order; الطُّلَّابُ كَانُوا مُسْتَعِدِّينَ is subject-first full agreement.
## كَانَ + present for past habit or ongoing action
This frame is extremely useful for narrating routines and background actions.

TABLE: Frame | Model | Meaning // past habit | كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. | I used to read every day. // past ongoing | كَانَتْ تَدْرُسُ عِنْدَمَا اتَّصَلْتُ. | She was studying when I called. // past description + action | كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا، وَكَانَ الْأَطْفَالُ يَلْعَبُونَ. | The weather was beautiful and the children were playing.
[callout/warning] Do not mechanically double the past: كُنْتُ دَرَسْتُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ does not normally express a simple repeated habit. Use كُنْتُ أَدْرُسُ .
## Core sisters for change and continuation
Each verb adds a specific meaning while keeping the kāna-style relationship.

TABLE: Verb | Meaning | Model // أَصْبَحَ | became / came to be, often morning context | أَصْبَحَ الْجَوُّ دَافِئًا. // صَارَ | became / changed into | صَارَ الطَّرِيقُ مُزْدَحِمًا. // ظَلَّ | remained / continued | ظَلَّ الْبَابُ مَفْتُوحًا. // مَا زَالَ | is still / continues to be | مَا زَالَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ مَفْتُوحَةً.
[callout] Meaning first: choose the sister because it expresses past state, change or continuation—not merely to make the sentence look advanced.
## Misconception clinic
Repair one feature at a time.

TABLE: Draft | Improved version | Reason // كَانَ الطَّقْسَ جَمِيلٌ. | كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا. | Noun nominative; single-word predicate accusative. // كَانَ هِيَ مُتْعَبَةٌ. | كَانَتْ مُتْعَبَةً. | Conjugate كَانَ; the pronoun may be omitted. // كُنْتُ دَرَسْتُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. | كُنْتُ أَدْرُسُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. | Past habitual frame uses present after كَانَ. // صَارَتِ الْمَدِينَةَ مُزْدَحِمَةٌ. | صَارَتِ الْمَدِينَةُ مُزْدَحِمَةً. | Same kāna-family case pattern. // زَالَتِ الْمُشْكِلَةُ صَعْبَةً. | مَا زَالَتِ الْمُشْكِلَةُ صَعْبَةً. | مَا is required in the common “still” construction.
## Game: Rebuild the time frame
Choose the form that expresses past state, habit, change or continuation.
## Skills workshop
Build a past description with background, change and continuing consequences.
[ar] عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرَةً، كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ، وَكَانَ الطَّرِيقُ هَادِئًا.
[ar] بَعْدَ بِنَاءِ الْمَحَطَّةِ، صَارَ الْحَيُّ مُزْدَحِمًا، وَلَكِنَّهُ مَا زَالَ جَمِيلًا.
### Then and now
Write 110–130 Arabic words comparing a place, routine or period in your life in the past and now.
[callout] Success checklist: Use four forms of كَانَ, one كَانَ + present habit, one صَارَ or أَصْبَحَ, one مَا زَالَ, and accurate time expressions.
[callout] Paper route: Draw a two-column “then/now” plan, write the paragraph, then underline every form from the kāna family.
## Final mastery check
Control past state, conjugation, habit and the main sisters.
### What you can now do
- Transform a present nominal sentence into a past state.
- Conjugate كَانَ for common persons and groups.
- Use كَانَ + present for past habits and ongoing actions.
- Express becoming and continuation with selected sisters.
Spaced revisit: record a one-minute “then and now” comparison without reading your paragraph.
